description: The Fire Pig in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1947 and 2007 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Pig is the Pig born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the twelfth animal. It combines the Pig's generosity with Fire's qualities. Fire Pig years between 1924 and 2044 are 1947 and 2007. The Pig's fixed element is Water.

sections.heading: The Fire Pig personality
paragraphs: A Fire year puts the Pig in an interesting position, because Water controls Fire and the Pig's fixed element is Water. The animal is said to restrain and channel the stem's heat, adding passion and drive to its gentle nature without letting the fire rage. Fire Pigs are commonly depicted as enthusiastic, brave and generous, with big appetites for life and a strong desire to succeed. They tend to be affectionate and energetic, putting heart into everything they do. The underlying tension can create emotional swings, however, and readings mention impulsiveness, a tendency to overindulge and a stubborn streak when their enthusiasm meets resistance. When they love an idea, they pursue it with their whole heart and expect others to keep up.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: Fire Pig at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

The Fire Pig brings appetite and enthusiasm to everything it touches. Restaurants, entertainment, sales, travel and festival management are typical arenas, as warmth and energy win customers there. It works hard in bursts, loves a team celebration and can talk a hesitant client round with genuine excitement. Over the long haul, though, it benefits from someone tracking the budget. In love the Fire Pig is passionate, demonstrative and generous to a fault, planning surprise feasts and weekend escapes. Honesty and plenty of affection keep it content. The recurring friction is indulgence: impulsive spending or a habit of saying yes to every invitation can strain a partner who prefers a quieter calendar.

sections.heading: Fire Pig years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Fire Pig years are 1947 (January 22, 1947 to February 9, 1948) and 2007 (February 18, 2007 to February 6, 2008). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 2007 anyone born before Feb 18 is a Fire Dog, not a Fire Pig. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Fire Pig year is Yin, matching the Pig's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Ding-Hai, joining the heavenly stem Ding to the earthly branch Hai. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Dog year (before January 22, 1947) and the Fire Dog year (before February 18, 2007), and births in the weeks after each Fire Pig year ends belong to the Earth Rat. The new year itself fell on a Wednesday in 1947 and Sunday in 2007.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Pig
paragraphs: For a Fire Pig, sustainable rhythms matter more than bursts of effort. Pacing ambitions, building rest into busy periods and practising moderation help their energy last. Because they act on enthusiasm, pausing to consider practical details prevents later regret. Fire Pigs often thrive in roles that combine generosity and initiative, such as entrepreneurship, events or caring leadership. Physical exercise helps steady their emotional swings. Listening carefully when others raise concerns, rather than pushing through, strengthens relationships. Balanced, Fire Pigs bring warmth and vitality to everyone they meet. Their enthusiasm is a gift worth protecting from exhaustion.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Pig shares the Pig's San He trine with the Rabbit and Goat (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Tiger, and its Liu Chong clash with the Snake. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Pig years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1947 (from January 22, 1947) and 2007 (from February 18, 2007). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Pig's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Pig's fixed element is Water; in the five-element cycles water controls Fire. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Pig?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rabbit and Goat (San He) and the Tiger (Liu He). The Snake is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Pig called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ding-Hai. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Ding, followed by its earthly branch, here Hai for the Pig, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Pig different from other Pigs?
faq.answer: All Pigs share generosity, sincerity and warmth. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
